sanskrit: nityaṃ kālaparītasya mama vā madvidhasya vā buddhir vyasanam āsādya bhinnā naur iva sīdati
english: For one ever encompassed by Time—be it I or one of my kind—the intellect, having met with calamity, sinks like a foundering ship.

sanskrit: ahaṃ ca tvaṃ ca ye cānye bhaviṣyanti surādhipāḥ te sarve śakra yāsyanti mārgam indraśatair gatam
english: I and you, and whatever others shall become lords of the gods—all of them, O Śakra, shall travel the road already trodden by a hundred Indras.

sanskrit: tvām apy evaṃ sudurdharṣaṃ jvalantaṃ parayā śriyā kāle pariṇate kālaḥ kālayiṣyati mām iva
english: Even you, so unassailable, blazing with supreme splendor—when the appointed time has ripened, Time shall drive you on as it has driven me.

sanskrit: bahūnīndrasahasrāṇi daiteyānāṃ yuge yuge abhyatītāni kālena kālo hi duratikramaḥ
english: Many thousands of Indras of the Daiteyas have passed away through Time, age after age; for Time is hard to transcend.

sanskrit: idaṃ tu labdhvā tvaṃ sthānam ātmānaṃ bahu manyase sarvabhūtabhavaṃ devaṃ brahmāṇam iva śāśvatam
english: Yet having gained this station, you hold yourself in high regard, as though you were the eternal god Brahmā, the source of all beings.

sanskrit: na cedam acalaṃ sthānam anantaṃ vāpi kasya cit tvaṃ tu bāliśayā buddhyā mamedam iti manyase
english: But this station is neither unshakable nor endless for anyone; you, with a childish mind, think, 'This is mine.'

sanskrit: aviśvāsye viśvasiṣi manyase cādhruvaṃ dhruvam mameyam iti mohāt tvaṃ rājaśriyam abhīpsasi
english: You trust in what is not to be trusted, and you deem the impermanent permanent; out of delusion you covet this royal fortune, thinking, 'This is mine.'

sanskrit: neyaṃ tava na cāsmākaṃ na cānyeṣāṃ sthirā matā atikramya bahūn anyāṃs tvayi tāvad iyaṃ sthitā
english: She is held to abide steadfast neither with you, nor with us, nor with others; having passed by many another, she rests for now with you.

sanskrit: kaṃ cit kālam iyaṃ sthitvā tvayi vāsava cañcalā gaur nipānam ivotsṛjya punar anyaṃ gamiṣyati
english: Having lingered with you for a little while, O Vāsava, this fickle one will forsake you and pass on to another, as a cow forsakes a drinking-trough.

sanskrit: rājalokā hy atikrāntā yān na saṃkhyātum utsahe tvatto bahutarāś cānye bhaviṣyanti puraṃdara
english: For the worlds of kings that have passed away are more than I can dare to number, and others, far more numerous than you, shall yet come to be, O Puraṃdara.

sanskrit: savṛkṣauṣadhiratneyaṃ sasaritparvatākarā tān idānīṃ na paśyāmi yair bhukteyaṃ purā mahī
english: This earth, with her trees and herbs and jewels, her rivers, mountains, and mines—I no longer see those who once enjoyed her of old.

sanskrit: pṛthur ailo mayo bhaumo narakaḥ śambaras tathā aśvagrīvaḥ pulomā ca svarbhānur amitadhvajaḥ
english: Pṛthu, Aila, Maya, Bhauma, Naraka, and Śambara likewise, Aśvagrīva and Pulomā, Svarbhānu of boundless banner,

sanskrit: prahrādo namucir dakṣo vipracittir virocanaḥ hrīniṣedhaḥ suhotraś ca bhūrihā puṣpavān vṛṣaḥ
english: Prahrāda, Namuci, Dakṣa, Vipracitti, Virocana, Hrīniṣedha and Suhotra, Bhūrihan, Puṣpavān, Vṛṣa,

sanskrit: satyeṣur ṛṣabho rāhuḥ kapilāśvo virūpakaḥ bāṇaḥ kārtasvaro vahnir viśvadaṃṣṭro 'tha nairṛtaḥ
english: Satyeṣu, Ṛṣabha, Rāhu, Kapilāśva, Virūpaka, Bāṇa, Kārtasvara, Vahni, Viśvadaṃṣṭra, and then Nairṛta,

sanskrit: ritthāhutthau vīratāmrau varāhāśvo ruciḥ prabhuḥ viśvajit pratiśauriś ca vṛṣāṇḍo viṣkaro madhuḥ
english: Riṭṭha and Huṭṭha, Vīra and Tāmra, Varāhāśva, the mighty Ruci, Viśvajit and Pratiśauri, Vṛṣāṇḍa, Viṣkara, Madhu,

sanskrit: hiraṇyakaśipuś caiva kaiṭabhaś caiva dānavaḥ daityāś ca kālakhañjāś ca sarve te nairṛtaiḥ saha
english: Hiraṇyakaśipu as well, and the Dānava Kaiṭabha, and the Daityas and the Kālakhañjas—all of them, together with the Nairṛtas.

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavaḥ pūrve pūrvatarāś ca ye daityendrā dānavendrāś ca yāṃś cānyān anuśuśruma
english: These, and many others, those of former times and of times yet earlier, lords of the Daityas and lords of the Dānavas, and still others of whom we have heard in tradition—

sanskrit: bahavaḥ pūrvadaityendrāḥ saṃtyajya pṛthivīṃ gatāḥ kālenābhyāhatāḥ sarve kālo hi balavattaraḥ
english: many former lords of the Daityas have abandoned the earth and departed, all of them struck down by Time; for Time is the stronger.

sanskrit: sarvaiḥ kratuśatair iṣṭaṃ na tvam ekaḥ śatakratuḥ sarve dharmaparāś cāsan sarve satatasatriṇaḥ
english: By all of them were hundreds of sacrifices offered—you are not the only one of a hundred rites; all of them were devoted to dharma, all unceasing in their sessions of sacrifice.

sanskrit: antarikṣacarāḥ sarve sarve 'bhimukhayodhinaḥ sarve saṃhananopetāḥ sarve parighabāhavaḥ
english: All ranged through the sky, all fought facing the foe, all were endowed with firm-knit frames, all had arms like iron bludgeons.

sanskrit: sarve māyāśatadharāḥ sarve te kāmacāriṇaḥ sarve samaram āsādya na śrūyante parājitāḥ
english: All wielded a hundred wiles, all of them roamed at will; of none of them, having joined battle, is it heard that he was vanquished.

sanskrit: sarve satyavrataparāḥ sarve kāmavihāriṇaḥ sarve vedavrataparāḥ sarve cāsan bahuśrutāḥ
english: All were intent on the vow of truth, all moved at their pleasure, all were devoted to the vows of the Veda, and all were deeply learned.

sanskrit: sarve saṃhatam aiśvaryam īśvarāḥ pratipedire na caiśvaryamadas teṣāṃ bhūtapūrvo mahātmanām
english: All those mighty ones attained sovereignty entire and unbroken, yet in those great-souled ones there was never of old any intoxication with their power.

sanskrit: sarve yathārthadātāraḥ sarve vigatamatsarāḥ sarve sarveṣu bhūteṣu yathāvat pratipedire
english: All gave according to desert, all were free of envy, all conducted themselves rightly toward all beings.

sanskrit: sarve dākṣāyaṇīputrāḥ prājāpatyā mahābalāḥ jvalantaḥ pratapantaś ca kālena pratisaṃhṛtāḥ
english: All were sons of Dakṣa's daughters, of the lineage of Prajāpati, of mighty strength, blazing and scorching with heat—and all were gathered up by Time.

sanskrit: tvaṃ caivemāṃ yadā bhuktvā pṛthivīṃ tyakṣyase punaḥ na śakṣyasi tadā śakra niyantuṃ śokam ātmanaḥ
english: And you too, when you have enjoyed this earth and must let her go again, you will not then be able, O Śakra, to master the grief within yourself.

sanskrit: muñcecchāṃ kāmabhogeṣu muñcemaṃ śrībhavaṃ madam evaṃ svarājyanāśe tvaṃ śokaṃ saṃprasahiṣyasi
english: Let go your longing for sensual delights, let go this intoxication born of fortune; only thus, when your own sovereignty is lost, will you endure the grief.

sanskrit: śokakāle śuco mā tvaṃ harṣakāle ca mā hṛṣaḥ atītānāgate hitvā pratyutpannena vartaya
english: In a time of sorrow do not grieve, and in a time of joy do not exult; abandoning the past and the future, live in the present moment.

sanskrit: māṃ ced abhyāgataḥ kālaḥ sadāyuktam atandritam kṣamasva nacirād indra tvām apy upagamiṣyati
english: If Time has now come upon me—ever vigilant, never slack—be patient, O Indra; before long it will come to you as well.

sanskrit: trāsayann iva devendra vāgbhis takṣasi mām iha saṃyate mayi nūnaṃ tvam ātmānaṃ bahu manyase
english: As if to terrify me, O lord of the gods, you cut me to pieces here with words; with me thus bound, you surely think much of yourself.

sanskrit: kālaḥ prathamam āyān māṃ paścāt tvām anudhāvati tena garjasi devendra pūrvaṃ kālahate mayi
english: Time first came upon me, and afterward it runs in pursuit of you; that is why you roar, O lord of the gods, now that I have already been struck down by Time.

sanskrit: ko hi sthātum alaṃ loke kruddhasya mama saṃyuge kālas tu balavān prāptas tena tiṣṭhasi vāsava
english: For who in the world is able to stand against me, wrathful, in battle? But mighty Time has come; therefore, O Vāsava, you stand unscathed.

sanskrit: yat tad varṣasahasrāntaṃ pūrṇaṃ bhavitum arhati yathā me sarvagātrāṇi nasvasthāni hataujasaḥ
english: That term, ending in a thousand years, must surely have run full—seeing how all my limbs are out of sorts, my vigor undone.

sanskrit: aham aindrac cyutaḥ sthānāt tvam indraḥ prakṛto divi sucitre jīvaloke 'sminn upāsyaḥ kālaparyayāt
english: I have fallen from the station of Indra; you are made Indra in heaven, to be honored in this bright and varied world of the living—all through the turning of Time.

sanskrit: kiṃ hi kṛtvā tvam indro 'dya kiṃ hi kṛtvā cyutā vayam kālaḥ kartā vikartā ca sarvam anyad akāraṇam
english: For by doing what are you Indra today, and by doing what have we fallen? Time is the maker and the unmaker; everything else is no cause at all.

sanskrit: nāśaṃ vināśam aiśvaryaṃ sukhaduḥkhe bhavābhavau vidvān prāpyaivam atyarthaṃ na prahṛṣyen na ca vyathet
english: Meeting with loss and ruin, with sovereignty, with pleasure and pain, with being and non-being, the wise man should neither rejoice nor be distressed beyond measure.

sanskrit: tvam eva hīndra vetthāsmān vedāhaṃ tvāṃ ca vāsava vikatthase māṃ kiṃ baddhaṃ kālena nirapatrapa
english: For you, O Indra, know us, and I know you, O Vāsava; why do you boast over me, bound as I am by Time, O shameless one?

sanskrit: tvam eva hi purā vettha yat tadā pauruṣaṃ mama samareṣu ca vikrāntaṃ paryāptaṃ tan nidarśanam
english: For you yourself know of old what manhood was mine in those days, and what prowess in battles—that is proof enough.

sanskrit: ādityāś caiva rudrāś ca sādhyāś ca vasubhiḥ saha mayā vinirjitāḥ sarve marutaś ca śacīpate
english: The Ādityas and the Rudras and the Sādhyas, together with the Vasus, were all vanquished by me, and the Maruts too, O lord of Śacī.

sanskrit: tvam eva śakra jānāsi devāsurasamāgame sametā vibudhā bhagnās tarasā samare mayā
english: You yourself know, O Śakra, that in the clash of gods and Asuras the assembled gods were shattered by me in battle through my onset.

sanskrit: parvatāś cāsakṛt kṣiptāḥ savanāḥ savanaukasaḥ saṭaṅkaśikharā ghorāḥ samare mūrdhni te mayā
english: And mountains, with their forests and their forest-dwellers, with crags and peaks, terrible to behold, were more than once hurled by me upon your head in battle.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu śakyaṃ mayā kartuṃ yat kālo duratikramaḥ na hi tvāṃ notsahe hantuṃ savajram api muṣṭinā
english: But what can I do, since Time is not to be transcended? It is not that I lack the will to slay you, thunderbolt and all, with a single fist.

sanskrit: na tu vikramakālo 'yaṃ kṣamākālo 'yam āgataḥ tena tvā marṣaye śakra durmarṣaṇataras tvayā
english: But this is no time for valor; a time for forbearance has come. Therefore I bear with you, O Śakra—I who am harder to bear with than you.

sanskrit: tvaṃ mā pariṇate kāle parītaṃ kālavahninā niyataṃ kālapāśena baddhaṃ śakra vikatthase
english: When the time has ripened, you boast over me, O Śakra—me encompassed by the fire of Time, fettered fast in the noose of Time.

sanskrit: ayaṃ sa puruṣaḥ śyāmo lokasya duratikramaḥ baddhvā tiṣṭhati māṃ raudraḥ paśuṃ raśanayā yathā
english: This is that dark Person, whom the world cannot transcend; terrible, he stands having bound me, as one binds a beast with a tether.

sanskrit: lābhālābhau sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ kāmakrodhau bhavābhavau vadho bandhaḥ pramokṣaś ca sarvaṃ kālena labhyate
english: Gain and loss, pleasure and pain, desire and wrath, being and non-being, slaying, bondage, and release—all is obtained through Time.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ kartā na kartā tvaṃ kartā yas tu sadā prabhuḥ so 'yaṃ pacati kālo māṃ vṛkṣe phalam ivāgatam
english: I am not the doer, nor are you the doer; the doer is he who is forever the Lord. This Time it is that ripens me, like a fruit come to ripeness on a tree.

sanskrit: yāny eva puruṣaḥ kurvan sukhaiḥ kālena yujyate punas tāny eva kurvāṇo duḥkhaiḥ kālena yujyate
english: The very deeds that a man, in doing, is joined by Time to pleasures—doing those same deeds again, he is joined by Time to pains.

sanskrit: na ca kālena kālajñaḥ spṛṣṭaḥ śocitum arhati tena śakra na śocāmi nāsti śoke sahāyatā
english: One who knows Time, when touched by Time, ought not to grieve. Therefore, O Śakra, I do not grieve; there is no help to be had in grief.

sanskrit: yadā hi śocatāṃ śoko vyasanaṃ nāpakarṣati sāmarthyaṃ śocato nāsti nādya śocāmy ahaṃ tataḥ
english: Since for those who grieve the grief does not draw away the calamity, and the grieving man has no power to mend it—therefore I do not grieve today.

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sahasrākṣo bhagavān pākaśāsanaḥ pratisaṃhṛtya saṃrambham ity uvāca śatakratuḥ
english: Thus addressed, the thousand-eyed lord, the chastiser of Pāka, drawing back his fury, the god of a hundred sacrifices spoke thus:

sanskrit: savajram udyataṃ bāhuṃ dṛṣṭvā pāśāṃś ca vāruṇān kasyeha na vyathed buddhir mṛtyor api jighāṃsataḥ
english: At the sight of my arm upraised with the thunderbolt and of Varuṇa's nooses, whose mind here would not waver—even Death's, when he sought to kill?

sanskrit: sā te na vyathate buddhir acalā tattvadarśinī bruvan na vyathase sa tvaṃ vākyaṃ satyaparākrama
english: Yet that mind of yours does not waver—unshaken, beholding the truth; you, O you of true prowess, do not falter even as you speak your word.

sanskrit: ho hi viśvāsam artheṣu śarīre vā śarīrabhṛt kartum utsahate loke dṛṣṭvā saṃprasthitaṃ jagat
english: For what embodied being in the world could dare to place his trust in possessions or in the body, having seen the world set forth upon its passing?

sanskrit: aham apy evam evainaṃ lokaṃ jānāmy aśāśvatam kālāgnāv āhitaṃ ghore guhye satatage 'kṣare
english: I too know this world to be just so, impermanent—cast into the terrible fire of Time, hidden, ever-moving, imperishable.

sanskrit: na cātra parihāro 'sti kālaspṛṣṭasya kasya cit sūkṣmāṇāṃ mahatāṃ caiva bhūtānāṃ paripacyatām
english: And in this there is no escape for any creature touched by Time, as the beings, both small and great, are ripened away.

sanskrit: anīśasyāpramattasya bhūtāni pacataḥ sadā anivṛttasya kālasya kṣayaṃ prāpto na mucyate
english: From Time—subject to no lord, never heedless, ever ripening beings, never turning back—he who has met his ruin is not set free.

sanskrit: apramattaḥ pramatteṣu kālo jāgarti dehiṣu prayatnenāpy atikrānto dṛṣṭapūrvo na kena cit
english: Heedful among the heedless, Time keeps watch over embodied beings; never has it been seen by anyone to be overcome, however great the effort.

sanskrit: purāṇaḥ śāśvato dharmaḥ sarvaprāṇabhṛtāṃ samaḥ kālo na parihāryaś ca na cāsyāsti vyatikramaḥ
english: Ancient, eternal, the law impartial toward all that bears life—Time is not to be evaded, nor is there any transgressing it.

sanskrit: ahorātrāṃś ca māsāṃś ca kṣaṇān kāṣṭhāḥ kalā lavān saṃpiṇḍayati naḥ kālo vṛddhiṃ vārdhuṣiko yathā
english: Days and nights and months, instants, kāṣṭhās, kalās, and moments—Time gathers them up against us, as a usurer heaps up his interest.

sanskrit: idam adya kariṣyāmi śvaḥ kartāsmīti vādinam kālo harati saṃprāpto nadīvega ivoḍupam
english: The man who says, 'This I shall do today, that I shall do tomorrow'—Time, when it has come, sweeps him away as a river's current carries off a raft.

sanskrit: idānīṃ tāvad evāsau mayā dṛṣṭaḥ kathaṃ mṛtaḥ iti kālena hriyatāṃ pralāpaḥ śrūyate nṛṇām
english: 'Just now indeed I saw him—how is it he is dead?'—such is heard the lament of men as they are borne away by Time.

sanskrit: naśyanty arthās tathā bhogāḥ sthānam aiśvaryam eva ca anityam adhruvaṃ sarvaṃ vyavasāyo hi duṣkaraḥ ucchrāyā vinipātāntā bhāvo 'bhāvastha eva ca
english: Possessions perish, and so do enjoyments, station, and sovereignty as well; all is fleeting and unstable, and resolve is hard to keep. Risings end in downfalls, and being abides only in the condition of non-being.

sanskrit: sā te na vyathate buddhir acalā tattvadarśinī aham āsaṃ purā ceti manasāpi na budhyase
english: That mind of yours does not waver—unshaken, beholding the truth; you do not even in thought take note: 'I once was, before.'

sanskrit: kālenākramya loke 'smin pacyamāne balīyasā ajyeṣṭham akaniṣṭhaṃ ca kṣipyamāṇo na budhyase
english: In this world overpowered by mightier Time and ripened thereby, though you are cast about with neither eldest nor youngest spared, you take no heed.

sanskrit: īrṣyābhimānalobheṣu kāmakrodhabhayeṣu ca spṛhāmohābhimāneṣu lokaḥ sakto vimuhyati
english: In envy, pride, and greed, in desire, wrath, and fear, in craving, delusion, and conceit, the world clings and is bewildered.

sanskrit: bhavāṃs tu bhāvatattvajño vidvāñ jñānataponvitaḥ kālaṃ paśyati suvyaktaṃ pāṇāv āmalakaṃ yathā
english: But you, knowing the truth of existence, learned, endowed with knowledge and austerity, behold Time as plainly as a myrobalan fruit upon your palm.

sanskrit: kālacāritratattvajñaḥ sarvaśāstraviśāradaḥ vairocane kṛtātmāsi spṛhaṇīyo vijānatām
english: Knowing the truth of Time's course, skilled in all the sacred sciences, you are, O son of Virocana, perfected in soul, to be envied by those who understand.

sanskrit: sarvaloko hy ayaṃ manye buddhyā parigatas tvayā viharan sarvatomukto na kva cit pariṣajjase
english: This whole world, I think, has been encompassed by your intellect; ranging at large, released on every side, you cling to nothing anywhere.

sanskrit: rajaś ca hi tamaś ca tvā spṛśato na jitendriyam niṣprītiṃ naṣṭasaṃtāpaṃ tvam ātmānam upāsase
english: For passion and darkness do not touch you, master of your senses; free of elation, your torment destroyed, you wait upon your own self.

sanskrit: suhṛdaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ nirvairaṃ śāntamānasam dṛṣṭvā tvāṃ mama saṃjātā tvayy anukrośinī matiḥ
english: Beholding you—a friend to all beings, free of enmity, serene of mind—there has arisen in me a heart of compassion toward you.

sanskrit: nāham etādṛśaṃ buddhaṃ hantum icchāmi bandhane ānṛśaṃsyaṃ paro dharmo anukrośas tathā tvayi
english: One so enlightened I do not wish to slay in his bondage; non-cruelty is the highest law, and so too is compassion toward you.

sanskrit: mokṣyante vāruṇāḥ pāśās taveme kālaparyayāt prajānām apacāreṇa svasti te 'stu mahāsura
english: These nooses of Varuṇa shall be loosed from you in the turning of Time, through the misconduct of mankind; may it be well with you, O great Asura.

sanskrit: yadā śvaśrūṃ snuṣā vṛddhāṃ paricāreṇa yokṣyate putraś ca pitaraṃ mohāt preṣayiṣyati karmasu
english: When the daughter-in-law shall set the aged mother-in-law to menial service, and the son out of folly shall send his father to do his tasks;

sanskrit: brāhmaṇaiḥ kārayiṣyanti vṛṣalāḥ pādadhāvanam śūdrāś ca brāhmaṇīṃ bhāryām upayāsyanti nirbhayāḥ
english: when the base-born shall make Brāhmaṇas wash their feet, and Śūdras shall take Brāhmaṇa women to wife without fear;

sanskrit: viyoniṣu ca bījāni mokṣyante puruṣā yadā saṃkaraṃ kāṃsyabhāṇḍaiś ca baliṃ cāpi kupātrakaiḥ
english: when men shall spill their seed into wombs not their own, bringing about confusion of castes, and shall offer oblation in bronze vessels and in unworthy vessels;

sanskrit: cāturvarṇyaṃ yadā kṛtsnam unmaryādaṃ bhaviṣyati ekaikas te tadā pāśaḥ kramaśaḥ pratimokṣyate
english: when the whole order of the four castes shall pass beyond its bounds—then, one by one, these nooses of yours shall be loosed in due succession.

sanskrit: asmattas te bhayaṃ nāsti samayaṃ pratipālaya sukhī bhava nirābādhaḥ svasthacetā nirāmayaḥ
english: From us you have nothing to fear; await the appointed time. Be happy, untroubled, sound of mind, and free of ill.

sanskrit: tam evam uktvā bhagavāñ śatakratuḥ; pratiprayāto gajarājavāhanaḥ vijitya sarvān asurān surādhipo; nananda harṣeṇa babhūva caikarāṭ
english: Having spoken thus to him, the lord of a hundred sacrifices set forth again, borne by the king of elephants; and the lord of the gods, having conquered all the Asuras, rejoiced in gladness and became sole sovereign.

sanskrit: maharṣayas tuṣṭuvur añjasā ca taṃ; vṛṣākapiṃ sarvacarācareśvaram himāpaho havyam udāvahaṃs tvaraṃs; tathāmṛtaṃ cārpitam īśvarāya ha
english: And the great sages straightway praised him, Vṛṣākapi, the lord of all that moves and moves not; the dispeller of cold bore up the oblation in haste, and so was the nectar of immortality offered up to the Lord.
